mcat_description.short: Prefabricated huts are factory-manufactured portable structures assembled from steel frames, FRP panels, PUF sandwich panels, or GI sheets, supplied as complete units or knock-down kits for rapid on-site erection. They are sold per piece or per sq ft to industrial, construction, and institutional buyers for temporary or semi-permanent accommodation and utility use.
mcat_description.long: Prefabricated huts are engineered portable structures where all major components — steel or GI frames, wall panels (PUF, FRP, GI colour-coated, or cement fibre board), roof panels, doors, and windows — are manufactured off-site in a factory and transported for quick bolted assembly at the destination. In the Indian B2B market, the dominant commercial form is a mild steel or GI-framed hut with insulated PUF or FRP panels, used as labour quarters, site offices, guard cabins, and temporary staff accommodation on construction and industrial sites. A secondary segment comprises bamboo and natural-material huts built for resort, eco-tourism, and hospitality applications, which differ fundamentally in construction method, buyer profile, and regulatory context. Structural compliance in the manufactured segment follows BIS/IS codes for steel detailing, wind load, and seismic zone requirements applicable to the project location.

market_context: In the Indian B2B market, prefabricated huts are primarily manufactured portable structures built from mild steel or GI frames combined with insulated wall and roof panels — PUF sandwich panels, FRP sheets, or colour-coated GI sheets being the most common cladding materials. The dominant commercial applications are labour accommodation colonies on construction and infrastructure sites, temporary site offices, and security/guard cabins for industrial and government use. Structural compliance follows BIS/IS codes for steel detailing, wind load, and seismic zone requirements, with manufacturers citing IS 2062 E250 steel grade as a common structural steel standard. A secondary and commercially distinct segment comprises bamboo and natural-material huts built for resort, eco-tourism, and hospitality buyers — these are handcrafted rather than factory-prefabricated and attract a fundamentally different buyer profile. Key manufacturing hubs include Delhi-NCR (Noida, Ghaziabad, Faridabad, Gurugram), Lucknow, Ahmedabad, and Vadodara. Sellers typically offer turnkey supply including design, fabrication, transport, and on-site erection. The market also includes a niche RPF/paramilitary segment (Railway Protection Force guard huts) visible in keyword data. Modular buildings may require local building permits, fire safety clearance, and structural compliance with BIS codes and local municipal regulations depending on project type and location (single source — low confidence for specific regulatory trigger thresholds).
